title: Complete the (1,2,4) Boolean fanout Pareto frontier: 31 vectors, six new (no new κ)
body:
## Result

For lee-phys's #5514 demand `(1,2,4)` over `F2^3`, the aggregate count vectors `(P_0,P_1,P_2; K_0,K_1,K_2)` (insertions, incoming ADDs) have exactly **31 Pareto-minimal elements**: the 25 vectors exposed by #5514's price envelope plus **six new unexposed vectors**

    P = e_i,   K = (2,2,2) + e_i + e_h,   h != i.

A one-insertion word may put its two extra ADDs in the insertion row and any other row, but never in both non-insertion rows: `K = (2,2,2) + e_j + e_k` with `i ∉ {j,k}` is impossible. This answers #5514 Open next question 1, including its suggested `(3,3,2)` first step.

Example (insertion row 0, extra ADD in row 2, `l_r` = lambda_r):

    E_02(l1+l2), E_20(l1+l2), E_01(l1), E_10(l1), P_0(g),
    E_10(l1), E_20(l1+l2), E_02(l1+l2), E_21(l1)

Each new vector costs the average of `U_(i,i)` and `U_(i,h)`, so it never uniquely minimizes a price, which is why the envelope cannot expose it.

**Claim type:** exact finite certificate for the one-insertion layer over `F2^3`, combined with #5514's written componentwise multi-insertion bounds (cited, not replayed). The six new words are proved for every Boolean ring with a nonzero orthogonal demand triple via the universal ring `F2^4`. No new κ, physical supplier or selected-frontier change.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

- All ADD-only words with at most four nonzero gates over `F2^3` (1, 42, 1111, 18472, 202192 distinct matrices for exactly 0–4 gates). No word with at most three gates splits `g e_i`, so each side of the insertion has exactly four gates when `sum K = 8`.
- For each root, 104 four-gate suffix matrices; pairing count vectors of the same matrix gives exactly the five totals `(2,2,2)+2e_h` and `(2,2,2)+e_i+e_h`. Root 0 classes: 56 doubled only in row 0, 20 only in row 1, 20 only in row 2, 4 each in `{0,1}` and `{0,2}`; none in `{1,2}`.
- Six new words replayed with a separate interpreter on formal columns over `F2^3` and `F2^4`, with reversed inverses, plus 24,576 literal width-one inputs. 17 mutation controls rejected.
- Nine-or-more-ADD one-insertion vectors shown dominated; the 31 vectors checked pairwise non-dominating.

Reproduce from the branch root (about one second each):

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/fanout-one-insertion-pareto/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/fanout-one-insertion-pareto/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fanout-one-insertion-pareto
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/fanout-one-insertion-pareto --check-source-history
```

Local results at `b6d49298b6ca5f40c47532866ae45dc16b8416ca`: both verifier modes print `PASS_FANOUT_ONE_INSERTION_PARETO` (≈1.05 s each); the registered runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`; the source-history check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

- The exclusion of non-root extra ADDs is certified over `F2^3` only; no written proof, and larger Boolean rings are open.
- The multi-insertion layer rests on #5514's written proof.
- Directed-edge prices, helpers, restricted coefficients and non-Boolean rings are outside scope. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Does the non-root exclusion hold over every Boolean ring with a nonzero orthogonal triple? Start with the four-gate enumeration over the universal ring `F2^4` (90 gates), or a written invariant.
- What is the frontier with independently priced directed edges (#5514 Open next question 2)? Start from the directed-edge multisets of the four-gate split words found here.

## Related open work

- #5933 (exact six-call nonunit fanout on a directed cycle): a different demand `(2,1,1)` over `Z/4` with directed-edge prices; no shared number.

## Credit

lee-phys #5514 supplies the question, contract, column and return lemmas, multi-insertion case analysis and 25 attaining words, with its credited lineage (#3063, #4916, #5163, #5139, #5259, #5304, Ali Romman #5310). New work: the exhaustive eight-ADD one-insertion decision, the six new words, the universal-ring transfer and the 31-vector frontier.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19220109
